newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: S&P comfortable with RBNZ's monetary policy stance.
newsitem.headline: S&P comfortable with RBNZ's monetary policy stance.

text.p: The Reserve Bank has not jeopardised New Zealand's AA plus sovereign debt rating by sanctioning the recent easing in monetary conditions, Standard and Poor's said on Tuesday.

Australia Managing Director Graeme Lee said S&P did not consider that the central bank's December Monetary Policy Statement, released this morning, had changed New Zealand's fundamental fiscal or monetary policy outlook.
"The statement is within the expectations that are underpinning New Zealand's sovereign rating," Lee told Reuters.

In a speech at the presentation of the bank's six-monthly policy statement, Governor Don Brash formally endorsed the recent easing in monetary conditions but warned markets of over-exuberance. Short term interest rates have rallied nearly 200 basis points since the October 12 election.
"We don't view those changes as a fundamental change in fiscal or monetary policy by the government or the Reserve Bank," Lee said.

He said S&P was not concerned that the new centre-right coalition government of National and New Zealand First, formed last Tuesday, had widened the Reserve Bank's target band for core inflation to 0-3 percent from 0-2 percent.

"The expectation that the inflationary band could be widened slightly, given a certain outcome of the election, was generally freely known in the market last time we undertook the rating review of New Zealand, so it's not something that in itself concerns us greatly," he said.
S&P would monitor New Zealand's direction under its coalition stewardship but was comfortable with the outlook.
"We're very interested in the direction of policy over the medium term and we still see New Zealand having a strong commitment to fiscal and monetary discipline," said Lee.

"There's a slight modification in the stance and the application, but we still believe that commitment to fiscal and monetary discipline is there and we see that generally within the expectations of the rating."
